summary: Discovered one source-grounded candidate for RDKit RECAP terminal molecular fragments. Saved the discovery record only; no skill package was authored.

candidates.name: rdkit-recap-terminal-fragments
candidates.capability: Obtain unique terminal molecular fragments with RDKit Recap.RecapDecompose(mol).GetLeaves(), preserving fragment SMILES and optional leaf molecule access.
candidates.boundary: Molecular fragmentation for a valid RDKit molecule, optionally parsed from SMILES; not descriptor calculation, synthetic feasibility assessment, or chemical validation. Default RECAP settings and independent per-molecule decompositions define the core scope. Invalid parsing or decomposition failures must remain errors, distinct from a successful empty leaf dictionary. Input preparation should require a nonempty SMILES string, reject a failed parse before decomposition, and explicitly define treatment of zero-atom or disconnected inputs; these edge cases are not specified by the supplied module.
candidates.value: Removes recurring confusion between immediate children, all descendants, and terminal fragments; explains unique SMILES keys, dummy attachment atoms, and valid empty results without substituting the original molecule as a fragment.
candidates.usage_path: In an already provisioned Docker container with Python and RDKit (Chem, Chem.Recap, rdChemReactions), parse SMILES with Chem.MolFromSmiles, check that a valid molecule was produced, call root = Recap.RecapDecompose(mol), then leaves = root.GetLeaves(). Use sorted(leaves.keys()) for stable presentation and leaves[smi].mol for RDKit molecule access. Keep '*' attachment markers. root.children contains immediate children; root.GetAllChildren() contains all descendants. Both differ from terminal leaves, and GetLeaves excludes the root even when it has no children. Dictionary keys describe unique fragments, not occurrence counts.
candidates.construction: Direct packaging of the existing RDKit interface and documented examples; no new fragmentation algorithm or vendored RECAP implementation is needed. The author stage can supply concise usage instructions, source-linked semantics and example expectations, plus prerequisite and invalid-input guidance. Any wrapper would be mechanical parsing, validation and serialization glue. Preserve applicable copyright/license notices if source material is copied. Host business execution is prohibited; future execution and checks belong only in Docker.

evidence.claim: Inspected document.py lines 31-56: module overview attributes RECAP to Lewell et al. (1998), explains hierarchy output, and demonstrates Chem.MolFromSmiles -> RecapDecompose -> GetLeaves. The example has 4 immediate children, 5 descendants and 3 terminal SMILES: '*C1CC1', '*c1ccc(OC)cn1', '*c1ccccc1*'; leaf.mol supplies the molecule.

Inspected document.py lines 97-118 and 134-138: nodes own mol/children/parents; GetLeaves builds a SMILES-keyed dictionary by traversing children and retaining nodes without children. An empty root.children therefore gives {}, not a singleton original molecule; repeated keys do not represent multiplicity.

Inspected document.py lines 146-213: RecapDecompose immediately serializes the input molecule, creates a root, iterates reaction products and returns the hierarchy. It has no explicit invalid-input parser or validation contract. Defaults are allNodes=None, minFragmentSize=0, onlyUseReactions=None; shared allNodes can reuse a previously stored node.

Inspected document.py lines 180-195 and tests at 231-235 and 279-293: default filtering rejects products whose SMILES reduce to empty/C/CC/CCC after removing dummy markers/empty branches. test2 expects CCCOCCC to have no children; testMinFragmentSize shows minFragmentSize=3 yields the unique leaf '*CCC' for CCCOCCC, while CCCOCC still has no children. A positive size threshold counts explicit atoms minus dummy markers and changes the default filtering branch.

Inspected document.py lines 63-86: dependencies are RDKit Chem and rdChemReactions; reaction SMARTS generate '*' endpoints. Lines 81-82 explicitly label aromatic nitrogen-aromatic carbon cleavage as outside the standard RECAP set, so this is the supplied RDKit implementation, not a claim of exact identity to every published RECAP rule.

Inspected document.txt, entire BSD 3-Clause license: source redistribution requires retained copyright, conditions and disclaimer; binary redistribution requires their reproduction; endorsement is restricted. document.py lines 1-29 carry a separate Novartis copyright and equivalent conditions.

gaps: No business code or tests were executed; example expectations are inspected source evidence, not independently verified results.

The supplied module does not document malformed-SMILES parsing, zero-atom inputs, or disconnected-input policy; the author must state a narrow input contract and keep parsing failures separate from valid empty fragments.

Installed RDKit availability/version and Docker prerequisites remain to be checked in the author/acceptance stage; runtime behavior should be tied to the provided commit or documented compatible version.
